court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Principal District Judge, Chengalpattu - CMA No.67/2003
facts_of_case: The wife filed a petition under Section 12(1)(c) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, for a decree of nullity of marriage. The husband had averred that the marriage was solemnized between the parties on 31.05.1996 as per Hindu Rites and Customs. The marriage was an arranged marriage and it was consummated.

legal_principles.principle: A party seeking to annul a marriage must follow the procedure laid down under Order 32 Rule 15 CPC.
legal_principles.held: petitioner while describing the respondent as a mentally ill person, he should have followed the procedure laid down under Order 32 Rule 15 CPC.

legal_principles.principle: A party's consent to marriage is not free and voluntary if obtained by suppression of material facts and playing fraud.
legal_principles.held: petitioner's consent to marriage was not free and voluntary, but obtained by suppression of material facts and by playing fraud
cited_cases: RAM NARAIN GUPTA VS. SMT. RAMESHWARI GUPTA

outcome.final_order: The decree and judgment made in CMA No.67/2003 passed by the Principal District Judge, Chengalpattu dated 25.11.2005 reversing the decree and judgment made in HMOP No.22 of 1997 on the file of the Principal Sub Court, Chengalpattu, dated 28.08.2002 was set aside, reversed and varied.

use_for_drafting: advising on Hindu Marriage Act implications
